```{r setup}
#| include: false
# Team cards are built from data/team-members.csv (one row per person).
# To add or update someone, edit the spreadsheet; this page rebuilds itself.
# Base R only, so no extra packages are needed.
team <- read.csv("data/team-members.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                 encoding = "UTF-8", na.strings = character(0))

# Escape HTML and write any non-ASCII character (é, ’, ·) as a numeric HTML
# entity, so the page is correct whatever locale R runs in.
esc <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("&", "&amp;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("<", "&lt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub(">", "&gt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  vapply(x, function(s) {
    cp <- utf8ToInt(enc2utf8(s))
    paste(ifelse(cp > 127, sprintf("&#%d;", cp), intToUtf8(cp, multiple = TRUE)), collapse = "")
  }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}
dot <- " &middot; "
has <- function(x) !is.na(x) && nzchar(trimws(x))
cap1 <- function(x) paste0(toupper(substring(x, 1, 1)), substring(x, 2))

# Expertise is one or more of the five discipline subgroups, separated by ";"
expertise_of <- function(x) {
  if (!has(x)) return(character(0))
  trimws(strsplit(x, ";", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
}

# one colour per discipline subgroup
tag_class <- function(x) {
  key <- c("Public health, infectious disease and epidemiology" = "tag-ph",
           "Environmental and physical sciences" = "tag-env",
           "Mathematical sciences" = "tag-math",
           "Social sciences" = "tag-soc",
           "Communication, knowledge translation and exchange" = "tag-comm")
  out <- unname(key[x]); out[is.na(out)] <- "tag-other"; out
}

orcid_icon <- '<svg class="orcid-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="12" fill="#a6ce39"/><text x="12" y="16" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" font-weight="700" fill="#fff" font-family="Arial, sans-serif">iD</text></svg>'

# badge: which column holds the role badge ("role" shows Co-chair; "working_role"
# shows the working group role)
card <- function(p, badge = "role") {
  name <- paste(p$first_name, p$last_name)
  out <- c('<div class="member-card">')
  # photo_style (optional) adjusts one person's photo crop, e.g. a centred crop
  # or extra space around a tightly framed headshot
  style <- if (has(p$photo_style)) sprintf(' style="%s"', esc(p$photo_style)) else ""
  out <- c(out, sprintf('<img class="member-photo" src="%s" alt="%s"%s>', p$photo, esc(name), style))
  out <- c(out, sprintf('<p class="member-name">%s</p>', esc(name)))
  if (has(p$post_nominals))
    out <- c(out, sprintf('<p class="member-creds">%s</p>', esc(p$post_nominals)))
  b <- p[[badge]]
  if (has(b) && b != "Member")
    out <- c(out, sprintf('<p><span class="member-badge">%s</span></p>', esc(b)))
  if (has(p$title))
    out <- c(out, sprintf('<p class="member-title">%s</p>', esc(p$title)))
  if (has(p$affiliation))
    out <- c(out, sprintf('<p class="member-aff">%s</p>', esc(p$affiliation)))
  # coloured tags: World Bank region first, then discipline subgroups
  # (public health, infectious disease and epidemiology always listed last)
  ex <- expertise_of(p$expertise)
  ex <- ex[order(ex == "Public health, infectious disease and epidemiology")]
  tags <- c(if (has(p$region)) sprintf('<span class="team-tag tag-region">%s</span>', esc(p$region)),
            sprintf('<span class="team-tag %s">%s</span>', tag_class(ex), esc(ex)))
  if (length(tags))
    out <- c(out, sprintf('<p class="member-tags">%s</p>', paste(tags, collapse = "")))
  if (has(p$term))
    out <- c(out, sprintf('<p class="member-meta">Executive group member, %s</p>', esc(p$term)))

  # text links, as on the POPCORN team page: ORCID, Web bio, COI form
  links <- character(0)
  if (has(p$orcid))
    links <- c(links, sprintf('<a class="orcid-link" href="https://orcid.org/%s" aria-label="ORCID iD for %s">%s ORCID</a>',
                              p$orcid, esc(name), orcid_icon))
  if (has(p$profile_url))
    links <- c(links, sprintf('<a href="%s">Web bio</a>', p$profile_url))
  if (has(p$coi_url))
    links <- c(links, sprintf('<a href="%s/?action=download" aria-label="Conflict-of-interest disclosure form for %s (PDF)">COI form</a>',
                              p$coi_url, esc(name)))
  if (length(links))
    out <- c(out, sprintf('<p class="member-links">%s</p>', paste(links, collapse = "")))

  if (has(p$bio)) {
    paras <- strsplit(p$bio, "\n\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
    out <- c(out, '<details class="declaration member-bio">', '<summary>Read bio</summary>',
             '<div class="declaration-body">',
             sprintf('<p>%s</p>', esc(paras)), '</div>', '</details>')
  }
  c(out, '</div>')
}

grid <- function(rows, cls = "team-grid", badge = "role") {
  cards <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(rows)), function(i) card(rows[i, ], badge)))
  cat(paste(c(sprintf('<div class="%s">', cls), cards, '</div>'), collapse = "\n"), "\n")
}

# Executive group members are shown in spreadsheet order: reorder the rows to change it
exec <- team[team$group == "executive", ]
# Study working group: everyone marked working_group = yes (principal investigator first)
working <- team[team$working_group == "yes", ]
working <- working[order(working$working_role == "", working$last_name), ]
past <- team[team$group == "past", ]

n_regions <- length(unique(exec$region[nzchar(exec$region)]))
n_expertise <- length(unique(unlist(lapply(exec$expertise, expertise_of))))

past_list <- function(rows) {
  items <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(rows)), function(i) {
    p <- rows[i, ]
    detail <- c(if (has(p$title)) p$title, if (has(p$affiliation)) p$affiliation,
                if (has(p$expertise)) paste(expertise_of(p$expertise), collapse = "; "))
    sprintf('<li><span class="past-name">%s</span> <span class="past-term">%s</span><br><span class="past-detail">%s</span></li>',
            esc(paste(p$first_name, p$last_name)), esc(p$term), paste(esc(detail), collapse = dot))
  }, character(1))
  cat(paste(c('<ul class="past-list">', items, '</ul>'), collapse = "\n"), "\n")
}
```

Our work on PHES-EF is led by an international collaborative group committed to transparency and rigour in the evaluation of public health environmental surveillance. Our team brings together expertise from diverse regions, disciplines, and actor and end-user perspectives.

## Executive group

The executive group oversees and supports the development of PHES-EF. Co-chaired by Doug Manuel and David Buckeridge, it brings together members from five World Bank regions and all five of the study's discipline subgroups: public health, infectious disease and epidemiology; environmental and physical sciences; mathematical sciences; social sciences; and communication, knowledge translation and exchange.

Members contribute by:

::: method-points
- Reviewing the candidate evaluation items for their organization, completeness, gaps and redundancy
- Advising the study working group in their areas of expertise
- Connecting the study with related projects and networks
- Helping identify e-Delphi panellists and promoting the survey among their professional contacts
- Taking part in the consensus meeting to agree on the final framework
- Guiding dissemination and promoting adoption of the framework among actors and end-users
:::

```{r executive}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
grid(exec)
```

## Study working group

The PHES-EF study working group, based at the Ottawa Hospital Research Institute, manages day-to-day research activities, coordinates the executive group, facilitates engagement with actors and end-users, and supports the implementation of all project components. The team moves the project forward through research coordination, knowledge synthesis, consultation with actors and end-users, and framework development.

